question: Should OpenClaw core provide a general agent-origin attestation mechanism for outbound HTTP requests, and what trust model and outbound paths should it cover?
rationale: This changes identity, signing, privacy, config, plugin/skill metadata, and outbound-request semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the product or security boundary.

options.title: Design a core attestation contract
options.body: Specify issuer/audience/signing/rotation/replay/privacy rules and the exact outbound paths before implementation.

options.title: Keep attribution provider-scoped
options.body: Decline general arbitrary-HTTP attestation for now and continue limiting built-in identity headers to verified provider integrations.

options.title: Route through plugins or service handshakes
options.body: Require external services to use plugin-owned or service-owned authentication unless maintainers approve a missing generic core API.

recommendation.title: Design a core attestation contract
recommendation.body: Specify issuer/audience/signing/rotation/replay/privacy rules and the exact outbound paths before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He provided the existing product/security keep-open review and appears in recent adjacent code history.
